lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Chris! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walks after dinner went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your energy been this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Tired, but okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I didn't do it. It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My kids is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walks after dinner fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat dinner at the same time every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, yes. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've been really tired.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know where the day goes. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The days got away from you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've got a plan in mind already.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Could someone in the family walk with you?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, let's say I take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 4.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 4 and not a 1?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 0 out of 3 days, the hard part was the rain, and next week you're going to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Oh, before you go, oh, and I've had a fever since last night. 101. I'm still on chemo.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Thank you for telling me. That's something your care team needs to hear today. I'm going to call the nurse line as soon as we hang up, and if it gets worse, please go to the ER or call 911.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, that's fine.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Blood sugar benefit stated after permission
Kids are the reason for change
Reflects deeper meaning of family motivation
Believes planning ahead makes it possible
Does not follow up on change talk
Repeats earlier advice verbatim, ignores knee concern
Feels better when sticking to it
Plans bigger lunch to manage hunger
Escalates fever to nurse line and gives ER guidance

flags.reason: Fever of 101 while on chemo disclosed. Coach escalated, but deferred the nurse call until after hang-up and did not confirm the participant would act right away or ask about other symptoms.
Repeated the same unsolicited benefit advice verbatim after the participant had declined it, ignoring the knee-pain barrier raised at line 46.
Participant said 'I can probably manage three days' at line 22; coach responded with an unrelated question about dinner timing instead of reinforcing the change talk.
Next contact time not resolved; participant asked for a later time and coach ended with 'Talk soon' without confirming.

score.summary: The coach reflected family motivation well and built a goal with barrier planning, but repeated unsolicited advice at line 45 after the participant declined it and missed change talk at line 22. The fever disclosure at line 57 was escalated to the nurse line, though the coach did not confirm immediate action.
strengths: Line 14: complex reflection linking the participant's kids to the motivation for change.
Line 18: emphasized autonomy by affirming the participant's own plan.
Line 37: complex reflection named the ambivalence about whether the effort is worth it.
Line 55: clear summary of the week's results and the new goal, with an invitation to correct it.
Line 58: took the fever disclosure seriously and gave clear ER/911 guidance.
coaching_tips: Line 45: after the participant said walking hurts their knees, avoid repeating the same advice; ask permission or explore the knee barrier first.
Line 23: respond to change talk like 'I can probably manage three days' with a reflection or affirmation before moving on.
Line 58: before ending, confirm the participant will call the nurse line now and ask about other symptoms.
Line 60: confirm a specific next-contact time that works, rather than ending with 'Talk soon.'
Line 31: build the goal around the participant's own number (3 days) rather than introducing 5 days.
